messages.text: I’ll package the barrel interface checks into a standalone script with source hashes and explicit limits, so they can be rerun alongside the native endcap validation.

The script’s first run passes at revision `476826f6`. It checks every same-layer stave against the proposed pickups and finds no intersections; the tightest bound is 1.285 mm to the proposed copper rail. I’m checking the script’s failure controls and exclusions before handing it over.

Added [barrel_interfaces.py]([redacted] the only file changed. No commit or retained report created.

Run:

```sh
python3 -B tools/short_strip_redesign/barrel_interfaces.py \
  --output build/short-strip-redesign/barrel-interfaces.json
```

Verified against `476826f6b369a34d9fef08e56cfae5dfcdcda32e`:

- **3,170,144 box comparisons; zero intersections.**
- Minimum rail bounds: **1.285266 mm** proposed, **1.283132 mm** old-rail benchmark.
- Minimum bearing-ring clearance: **7.707659 mm**.
- Minimum straight-pipe contact length: **58.666667 mm**.
- SAT controls and negative window/source-hash controls passed.

The 10.4 kB report includes input/source/producer hashes, actual counts and exclusions. It explicitly identifies source-only inference, conditional CSG/contact assumptions and missing native barrel validation. Producer SHA-256: `fac476bcd701224eae1d24e976cc96b59f8e6f3cd166b2bc573fb5b0f58a031e`.
